Make a form
A form groups inputs. Give each input a label, and let "required" and the input type do the checking for you.
form input label submit text field email password required

<form>
  <label>Email <input type="email" name="email" required></label>
  <label>Password <input type="password" name="password" minlength="6" required></label>
  <button>Sign in</button>
</form>

Change text colour and size
Colour and size are set in CSS. "color" is the text colour; "font-size" is best given in rem, so that it follows the reader's own settings.
text colour color font size bigger smaller bold style

Change the background
The background of the page is set on "body". It can be a colour, a gradient or an image.
background colour color gradient image page body

Put things side by side
Flexbox lays things out in a row. "gap" is the space between them, and "flex: 1" lets an item take the room that is left.
flex flexbox row side by side columns layout horizontal next to gap

Make a page work on phones
Add the viewport line to the head, use widths that can shrink, and change the layout under a certain width with a media query.

Animate something
A transition animates a change between two states. For a movement that runs by itself, use keyframes.

Dark mode
Keep the colours in variables, and give them other values when the device asks for a dark theme.

Use a custom font
Name the fonts you would like in order; the browser takes the first one it has. "system-ui" is the device's own font and needs no download.
font family typeface custom google system text

Link a stylesheet and a script
The stylesheet goes in the head. The script goes at the end of the body, or anywhere with "defer", so that the page exists when it runs.
link css stylesheet script js file connect include external defer

<head>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
  <script src="app.js" defer></script>
</head>
